subject: Private deployment: keystore custody, subprocessors, and access boundaries
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@orthohealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@orthohealth.com, procurement@orthohealth.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Private deploy questions — keystore, operator access, and jurisdictional controls

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week. We are tightening the security bar for any private deployment (VPC/on-prem) and have a few specific asks before we move forward with a pilot:

1) Customer keystore options — we need a clear statement of options (customer-managed KMS with HSM, customer-owned key material with Redwood only holding escrow, or Redwood-managed keys). For the latter two, please describe operator access and any scenarios where Redwood could decrypt or export keys.

2) Subprocessor list & roles — we require an up-to-date list of subprocessors involved in the private deployment flow (monitoring, logging, backup, telemetry) and whether those subprocessors process any plaintext customer inputs.

3) Data residency and cross-border transfers — deployment will be EU-only. Confirm whether any telemetry, diagnostics, or crash reports may transit through non-EU regions and what controls exist to prevent that.

4) Break-glass/incident access — outline the break-glass workflow, approvals required, and audit logging for any emergency operator access to customer environments.

I've attached a high-level network diagram and the relevant sections of our DPA for redline. Can we get a written summary and a 30–45 minute technical call next week (ideally Dec 3 or 4 CET)?

Appreciate it —
Alice Chen
Head of Security, OrthoHealth

Attachments: network-diagram-orthohealth-vpc.png, ortho_dpa_excerpt.pdf
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@orthohealth.com>
Cc: security@orthohealth.com, procurement@procurement.orthohealth.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 18:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions — keystore, operator access, and jurisdictional controls

Alice — thanks for the clear list, and totally understand the requirements. Summary and immediate answers below; I also included next steps and a proposed schedule.

Quick summary of keystore options (short):
- Customer-managed KMS (recommended): Customer keys stay in your KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / on-prem HSM). Redwood never has key material; we support envelope encryption where customer KMS signs or unwraps tokens at runtime.
- Customer-owned key with Redwood escrow: Customer provides key material; Redwood stores in encrypted escrow for emergency recovery. Access requires multi-party approvals and is strictly audited. Redwood will not export keys normally.
- Redwood-managed keys (not preferred for regulated data): Redwood holds key material in our KMS. Access limited to break-glass only; logs and justifications retained.

Operator access & what we do not access:
- Redwood operator/service accounts will not have routine access to decrypted customer inputs or model-trained artifacts.
- Operator activities include orchestration, node health checks, and limited runtime telemetry (CPU/GPU metrics, error traces). No plaintext prompt/response telemetry unless explicitly enabled by the customer for debugging.

Subprocessors (high level) — will send canonical list in follow-up and in the DPA appendix. Short list: cloud provider (for Dedicated control plane when requested), logging/alerting partner (aggregated metrics only), SRE tooling vendor (error aggregation). None of these subprocessors will have legitimate reason to access plaintext customer prompts in a private VPC deployment.

Telemetry and EU residency:
- For EU-only deployments we can configure regional endpoints and ensure telemetry ingestion points are EU-located. Crash dumps and diagnostic payloads are not sent outside EU unless the customer opts in.

Break-glass process (short):
- Customer must raise a break-glass request via the secure portal + sign an emergency access affidavit. Two-person Redwood approval (Engineering Lead + Security Lead) required and a signed time-bound access token issued. All actions are recorded to immutable audit logs and forwarded to the customer's SIEM via configured syslog/S3.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical sync — Thu Dec 3, 10:00–10:45 CET (I can do this).
2) I will circulate a draft DPA redline that includes the KMS language and an initial subprocessor appendix (attached).
3) We accept your network diagram and will confirm the VPC peering/VPN options.

I attached a short DPA redline and the canonical subprocessor list for initial review. If that looks OK I'll pull Marissa (Legal) and Rishi (Product Security) into the call.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-redline-2026-12-02.pdf
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0500
Subject: Fw: Private deploy questions — keystore, operator access, and jurisdictional controls

Folks — forwarding OrthoHealth's asks (below). They are explicit about EU-only residency and want strong assurances on KMS custody + break-glass.

Key asks we should cover on the call:
- Concrete DPA language for: customer-managed KMS; escrow mechanics and escrow access approval workflow; irreversible deletion obligations; subprocessors that handle any encrypted artifacts; and telemetry partitioning for EU-only deployments.
- Rishi: can you confirm whether our runtime ever writes model checkpoint or inferred artifacts to any shared storage that could be accessed by Redwood ops? I'd like a one-liner we can put into the DPA re: model artifact exposure.
- Kimberly / Marissa: any quick notes on whether the escrow wording below will need an addendum or separate keystore schedule?

Alice is available Dec 3 (CET) for a short sync. I'll coordinate once we have internal alignment on the KMS wording.

Subject: Re: Private deploy questions — keystore, operator access, and jurisdictional controls

Alice — quick follow-up after internal alignment. Thanks for sharing the diagram. Two attachments included: 1) a focused DPA redline that includes the KMS schedule and escrow mechanics; 2) a short subprocessor appendix. High level commitments below so you have it in writing before the call:

1) Custody options (finalized):
- Customer-managed KMS (Default for OrthoHealth): We will integrate with your KMS via envelope encryption. Redwood will never store key material.
- Escrow option (by request): Redwood will hold encrypted escrow in our EU tenant; escrow access requires written, signed dual-approval with a copy to OrthoHealth security and will be logged and auditable.
- Redwood-managed KMS: Only on explicit contractual exception; documented break-glass and audit requirements will apply.

2) Operator access boundaries:
- No routine access to plaintext prompts or responses.
- Operator activity limited to orchestration, patching, and runtime instrumentation (metrics only).
- Break-glass is time-limited, approved by two Redwood approvers, and recorded to immutable logs that are mirrored to your SIEM.

3) Subprocessors & telemetry:
- Appendix attached lists subprocessors and roles. For EU-only deployments we will route telemetry to EU endpoints; no crash dumps or diagnostic payloads will be sent outside EU without explicit opt-in.

4) DPA deliverables for the call:
- Finalized redline (attached) with an explicit KMS schedule and subprocessors appendix.
- Proposed language for escrow access + deletion obligations.

Proposed meeting: Fri Dec 3, 15:00–15:30 CET. If that works I'll send an invite and include Marissa (Legal) and Rishi (Product Security).

Best,
Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
